subject: General Knowledge
topic: Classical & folk dances of India — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Manipuri classical dance is most strongly rooted in which devotional tradition?

options.option_text: The Ras Lila — Krishna's circular dance with the Gopis of Vrindavan
The cosmic dance of Lord Shiva (Nataraja) and its tandava aspects
The ten incarnations of Vishnu narrated through Dashavatara episodes
The heroic episodes from the Mahabharata war fought at Kurukshetra

questions.explanation: Manipuri is a Vaishnavite dance; its defining performances are the Ras Lila, depicting Krishna's divine play with the Gopis. Maharaja Bhagyachandra of Manipur standardised these Ras performances in the 18th century. Shiva's Tandava (option B) is associated with Bharatanatyam's Nataraj imagery, not Manipuri.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three recognised regional styles of the Chhau dance?

options.option_text: Seraikella Chhau, from the Seraikella-Kharsawan district, Jharkhand
Purulia Chhau, practised in the Purulia district of West Bengal
Bastar Chhau, associated with the tribal belt of Chhattisgarh state
Mayurbhanj Chhau, native to the Mayurbhanj district of Odisha

questions.explanation: The three UNESCO-recognised Chhau styles are Seraikella (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal), and Mayurbhanj (Odisha). 'Bastar Chhau' does not exist — Chhattisgarh has distinct tribal art forms but no Chhau variant. Chhau was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

questions.stem: The 'Tribhangi' posture — a triple flexion of neck, torso, and knee forming an S-curve — is the defining sculptural aesthetic of which classical dance?

options.option_text: Bharatanatyam, characterised by the 'Araimandi' (half-seated) stance
Kuchipudi, known for dancing on the rim of a brass plate (tarangam)
Manipuri, distinguished by its soft, gliding, lyrical body movements
Odissi, whose grammar is visually built on this S-shaped body deflection

questions.explanation: Tribhangi (three bends) is the aesthetic cornerstone of Odissi, visually encoded in the sculptures of Konark and Lingaraj temples, which served as the revival grammar in the 20th century. Bharatanatyam's defining stance is the Araimandi (half-sitting), not Tribhangi, making option A the most tempting wrong answer.

questions.stem: The Kuchipudi dance form takes its name from a village in Andhra Pradesh whose Brahmin families were granted land by a Nawab of Golconda to perform it. Which option correctly identifies the village and the patron?

options.option_text: Kondapalli village in the Krishna district, famous for wooden toy crafts
Amaravati village near Guntur, a historic Buddhist site on the Krishna river
Kuchipudi village in the Krishna district, granted by Abul Hasan Tana Shah
Tirupati village in Chittoor district, home to the Tirumala Venkateswara temple

questions.explanation: Kuchipudi is named after Kuchelapuram (Kuchipudi) village in Krishna district. Nawab Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Golconda granted the village to Brahmin families (Bhagavathulus) for performing this dance-drama, codified by Siddhendra Yogi in the 17th century. Kondapalli (option A) is a nearby village famous only for lacquer toys.

questions.stem: The 'Gotipua' tradition of Odisha — young boys dressed as women performing acrobatic devotional movements — is regarded as one of the two main precursor streams of which classical dance?

options.option_text: Odissi, which synthesised the Gotipua and Mahari (Devadasi) traditions
Bharatanatyam, which evolved from the Devadasi tradition of Tamil Nadu
Manipuri, whose male performers enact female Gopi roles in the Ras Lila
Kuchipudi, performed exclusively by male Brahmin artists until the 20th century

questions.explanation: Odissi's classical form emerged from two streams: the Mahari tradition (female Devadasis in Jagannath temple) and the Gotipua tradition (boy-dancers performing acrobatic compositions). Option D is a plausible distractor because Kuchipudi was also historically male-only, but it has no connection to Gotipua. Bharatanatyam's Devadasi precursor is the Sadir tradition, not Gotipua.

questions.stem: The 'Ankiya Nat' one-act plays that form the theatrical foundation of Sattriya dance were composed by Srimanta Shankardev in which literary language?

options.option_text: Sanskrit, the liturgical language of all classical Indian dance-dramas
Maithili, the court language of the Koch kingdom that patronised Shankardev
Assamese, the vernacular language of the Ahom kingdom of medieval Assam
Brajawali — a literary blend of Braj Bhasha and Assamese coined by Shankardev

questions.explanation: Shankardev deliberately composed the Ankiya Nat in 'Brajawali', a hybrid literary language mixing Braj Bhasha (the devotional idiom associated with Krishna bhakti) with Assamese, making the Vaishnava content accessible to the masses. Sanskrit (option A) was the liturgical language of formal texts but Shankardev rejected it for popular devotional drama. Assamese alone (option C) is the most tempting wrong answer.

questions.stem: In which Manipuri performing tradition does the male artist play the barrel-shaped 'Pung' drum continuously while simultaneously executing acrobatic leaps and rotations — making the drum itself a choreographic element rather than mere accompaniment?

options.option_text: Cholom sub-style where the Kartal (cymbal) player leads the ensemble
Pung Cholom, where drum-playing and dancing are fused into a unified art
Sankirtana, the congregational singing and movement tradition of the Vaishnavs
Nupa Pala, a feminine lyrical form using only gentle hand gestures and steps

questions.explanation: Pung Cholom is the Manipuri style in which the male dancer plays the Pung (barrel drum) while performing acrobatic movements — the drum is an integral choreographic prop. Option C (Sankirtana) is the broader Manipuri Vaishnava tradition that includes Pung Cholom as a sub-component; UNESCO recognised Sankirtana in 2013, but Sankirtana is not synonymous with Pung Cholom specifically.
